record.exact_statement: For every fixed finite residual cube with a fixed interior product measure and fixed Boolean sign children G,H, let X be independent Bernoulli(p), F_p=G when X=1 and H when X=0, M_p=H(S_X|S_residual) and J_p=I(X;T) in the physical-child/spectral experiment, in bits. If a=hat G,b=hat H,D=support(b),A=sum_D a_T^2,c=E[GH], then J_p-M_p=2(c-A)p log2(1/p)+O_{G,H,measure}(p), and 1/2-2(c-A)=2||P_D a-c b||_2^2+2(c-1/2)^2. Therefore -4<=2(c-A)<=1/2, and the supremum over fixed actual Boolean pairs of the limiting coefficient equals 1/2. Equality holds exactly when c=1/2 and P_D a=b/2, realized by H=1,G=(-1)^(y1*y2) on two uniform residual bits. No dimension-uniform remainder or exchange of supremum and limit is asserted.

record.exact_statement: For every finite Boolean sign under any interior product measure, any singleton physical block X with bias p, and Shannon entropy in bits, let M_X=H(S_X|S_residual), J_X=I(X;T) in the actual physical-child/spectral experiment, r=min(p,1-p), and delta=1-sqrt(1-r). Then J_X-M_X<=h2(r)-h2(delta). The bound is uniform in dimension, residual biases and Boolean children. Consequently lim_{p->0} sup_{all finite actual Boolean signs and all interior residual product biases}(J_X-M_X)/(p log2(1/p))=1/2. The tax expansion is (r/2)log2(1/r)+((log2(e)-1)/2)r+O(r^2 log(1/r)); exact optimal tax at arbitrary nonzero p and influence/composition payment remain unproved.
